claim:
For every integer \(d\ge 1\) and every integer \(h\ge 2\), let \(F(z)=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^d}c_\varepsilon z^\varepsilon\) on normalized Haar \(\mathbb T^d\). Then
\[
\|F\|_{L^{2h}(\mathbb T^d)}^{2h}\le \left(2^{-h}\binom{2h}{h}\right)^d\left(\sum_\varepsilon |c_\varepsilon|^2\right)^h.
\]
The constant is sharp, so \(K_{2h}(\{0,1\}^d)=\left(2^{-h}\binom{2h}{h}\right)^{d/(2h)}\). For a nonzero coefficient family, equality holds if and only if there are \(\lambda\ne0\) and phases \(|\eta_j|=1\) such that \(c_\varepsilon=\lambda\prod_{j=1}^d\eta_j^{\varepsilon_j}\); equivalently, \(F(z)=\lambda\prod_{j=1}^d(1+\eta_jz_j)\).

correctness.rationale: The exact Hilbert-valued one-coordinate expansion has nonnegative coefficients.
